Since the entity is a Taiwan-registered WFOE with mainland Chinese UBOs, both Taiwan and China cross-strait regulations apply.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening must be performed against the Taiwan Ministry of Justice Economic Division PEP database, the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission AML unit, the Mainland China Central Discipline Inspection Commission archives for cross-strait PEPs, and international lists including UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and HMTF sanctions. Each UBO, director, and authorized signatory must be individually screened at onboarding and continuously monitored. Due diligence must include full-name matching with fuzzy/traditional-character variant analysis, source-of-wealth verification for all political connections, and documented risk escalation for any hit. Negative news and adverse media checks via independent databases are required. All screening results must be retained for at least five years in the company's AML/CFT file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval Online System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names in Taiwan must be in Traditional Chinese and/or English. The Chinese name must not be identical or similar to any previously registered name. English names, if used, must be phonetically transliterated from the Chinese name or otherwise not confusingly similar to existing English trade names. The naming convention follows a four-tier format: (1) geographic suffix, (2) trade name, (3) general business descriptor, (4) legal form suffix 'Limited Company' (有限公司). For foreign-invested WFOEs, the English name may include a phonetic transliteration of the Chinese name or a distinct trade name, subject to MOEA pre-approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Department of Commerce of MOEA within 30 days from the date of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the grounds for contesting the refusal, include a copy of the rejection decision, the original pre-approval application, and any supporting documents demonstrating that the proposed name does not violate the Trade Names Act or Business Registration Act. MOEA must render a decision within two months. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may petition for an administrative remedy at the Taipei High Administrative Court. An extension of the name reservation may be requested before expiry, subject to a filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Taiwan's Company Act requires a registered office address where statutory records are kept. For POD retail operations, Taiwanese tax authorities and large commercial banks generally reject pure virtual offices or commercial mailbox addresses as the sole registered address due to the need for physical inspection of inventory and financial records. A serviced office or co-working space with a physical presence, dedicated meeting rooms, and a reception area may be accepted, provided the address is not classified as a 'mailbox' and the company can demonstrate operational substance, such as payroll, equipment, and inventory storage. Banks require an actual business address for opening corporate bank accounts and for processing Stripe/PayPal settlements. Unannounced inspections by the National Taxation Bureau are possible; we quantify the likelihood as 'low to moderate' (30-50%) for e-commerce entities using a shared workspace with adequate local staffing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Confirm the registered office has a visible company nameplate; (2) Maintain employee workspace and retail-related equipment; (3) Keep inventory samples or order records on site; (4) Ensure original statutory books are available at the registered office. Quantified risk: National Taxation Bureau and MOEA conduct unannounced inspections for e-commerce businesses with 30-50% annual probability. Risk is mitigated by maintaining a leased serviced-office presence in Taipei City and hiring at least one resident accounting officer.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), particularly Articles 1, 2, 5, 98, 100, 101, 128, 129, 156, 161, 162, 172, 192, 193, 203, 208, 218, 228, 230, 387 and 449; construed together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 6, 7, and 8, and the Regulations for Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, through the MOEA One-Stop Online Application System; local municipal commercial registration office for the registered office, including the Taipei City Government Commercial Registration Office where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form and Articles of Incorporation, filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Company Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an ordinary retail/service company in Taiwan; however, the subscribed capital must be fully paid in at incorporation, deposited in a Taiwan banking institution in a capital subscription account in the company's name, and verified by a certified public accountant. No blocking escrow is required, but the capital funds must remain in the capital account and may not be withdrawn for operating expenses until the company registration certificate has been issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND ALL DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD

WHEREAS, the Company is to be incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise organized as a limited liability company under the Company Act of the Republic of China; and

WHEREAS, the Company intends to engage in online print-on-demand custom merchandise retailing, including the sale of custom apparel and related goods through internet-based platforms and payment rails; and

WHEREAS, the laws of Taiwan require the establishment of share capital, the designation of a registered office within the territory of Taiwan, the appointment of statutory officers, and the opening of corporate banking accounts before the Company can commence lawful operations; and

WHEREAS, the undersigned constitute the sole shareholder and all persons who shall serve as the first directors of the Company.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. Subscription and Allotment of Share Capital. The authorized share capital of the Company shall be New Taiwan Dollars Ten Million (NT$10,000,000), divided into One Million (1,000,000) shares with a par value of NT$10 per share. The sole shareholder is authorized and directed to subscribe for all issued shares for cash. The directors are authorized to open a capital subscription account with a licensed bank in Taiwan, to receive all capital contributions, to procure a capital verification report from a certified public accountant, and to take all steps necessary to evidence full payment of the subscribed capital.

2. Banking and Treasury Authorization. The directors are authorized to select and engage the Company's principal bankers, to open operating, foreign currency, payroll, and reserve accounts, and to execute all account opening agreements, mandates, electronic banking arrangements, and treasury documents. All cheques, drafts, wire transfers, and payment instructions shall be signed by two duly authorized directors, or by the managing director together with one director, as required by the Company's internal control policies.

3. Registered Office and Company Seal. The registered office of the Company shall be at the address set out in the Articles of Incorporation, within the territory of Taiwan. The directors are authorized to execute the lease, obtain landlord consent, file the office address with the competent authority, and adopt a company seal and chop, with specimen impressions to be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and all relevant government agencies.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following persons are appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company: one individual as Chairperson and Managing Director; one individual as Director and General Manager; and one individual as Compliance Officer and Corporate Secretary. Each appointed officer is authorized to represent the Company before the Ministry of Economic Affairs, tax authorities, labor authorities, banks, and other government offices within the scope of the Company's registered business.

5. General Authority and Ratification. The officers and directors are directed to prepare, execute, and file all applications, declarations, affidavits, and instruments necessary to obtain company registration, tax registration, foreign investment approval, and any other permits required under law. All acts performed in the name of the Company prior to the date of this resolution are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved.

This resolution is effective immediately and may be relied upon by all third parties dealing with the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment Approval from the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan; online filing through the MOEAIC e-Service portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an investment application to the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs through the official electronic system before incorporating the Taiwan entity. The application must identify the beneficial owner, proposed paid-up capital, source of funds, precise business scope corresponding to ISIC 4791, and the intended location of the registered office. The Investment Commission will screen the project against the negative list for mainland China investment and other restrictions applicable to foreign nationals. Because online retailing of custom apparel is an unrestricted activity, the approval letter is normally issued after document review. Any foreign corporate documents must be notarized or apostilled and accompanied by verified Chinese or English translations if required. The approval letter is an essential prerequisite for opening a bank account in the Company's name and for the subsequent company registration.
required_dossiers: Investment application form prescribed by the Investment Commission
Board resolution or power of attorney of the foreign investor
Certificate of incorporation and articles of association of the foreign investor
Passport or national identity card of the ultimate beneficial owner
Bank reference letter or evidence of source of funds
Projected business plan and capital expenditure summary
Specimen signature and seal card of the proposed Taiwan representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the foreign investor must respond to the deficiency notice through the MOEAIC online correction portal within 30 days, with supporting evidence. If the rejection relates to business scope ambiguity, the applicant may narrow the scope and resubmit. If the Investment Commission issues a formal adverse decision, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Executive Yuan within 30 days of service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs; Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before incorporation, the applicant must submit a company name and business scope pre-approval application to the central company name reservation system maintained by the Department of Commercial Affairs. The proposed name must be distinctive and must not conflict with any existing registered company name or trademark. The business scope must be drafted to cover internet retailing and print-on-demand custom merchandise sales, consistent with ISIC 4791 and Taiwan's Standard Industrial Classification. Once approved, the name reservation is valid for six months and may be extended once before expiration. The applicant must incorporate the exact approved name and business scope into the Articles of Incorporation. If the application is rejected for confusing similarity, the applicant may file a revised name within the prescribed period without additional administrative charges.
required_dossiers: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval Application
Copy of the applicant's passport or national identity card
Foreign investment approval letter from MOEAIC
Power of attorney authorizing the local agent to file the application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, file a new name application with a revised distinctive element within 10 days. If the business scope is rejected, narrow the wording and resubmit. A formal refusal may be appealed to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Subscription Bank Account and Obtain CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan and a certified public accountant registered with the Financial Supervisory Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving foreign investment approval, the Company must remit the approved capital from abroad into Taiwan through authorized banking channels. The remittance must be reported to the Central Bank of China under the foreign exchange regulations, and the bank must issue a foreign exchange remittance certificate. The funds shall be deposited into a dedicated capital subscription account opened in the name of CN_WFOE_LTD. After deposit, the bank issues a balance certificate. The Company then appoints a certified public accountant to examine the subscription statement, bank deposit certificate, remittance records, and proposed Articles, and to issue a capital verification report confirming that the issued capital has been fully paid in. The capital must remain in the account until the company registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment approval letter from MOEAIC
Foreign exchange remittance certificate from the remitting bank
Bank deposit balance certificate
Share subscription statement signed by the sole shareholder
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney for bank account signatories
Passport and Taiwan resident certificate of the company representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines account opening due to anti-money laundering concerns, submit an enhanced beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-wealth explanation. If the CPA notices a mismatch between the remittance amount and the subscribed capital, obtain a corrected remittance or execute an amended subscription schedule and reapply for verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Company Registration with MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs; local municipal commercial registration office based on the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company must file the complete company registration application through the MOEA One-Stop Online Application System. The filing package must include the approved name reservation, Articles of Incorporation, CPA capital verification report, bank balance certificate, foreign investment approval letter, registered office lease and landlord consent, and identity documents of the directors and officers. The registrar will review the legal form, capital structure, business scope, and compliance with the Company Act. Once approved, the Ministry of Economic Affairs issues the Company Registration Certificate. After issuance, the Company is deemed a legal person and may open general operating accounts, sign contracts, and commence business. The company seal must be filed with the registration authority.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Approved Articles of Incorporation
CPA capital verification report
Bank deposit balance certificate
Registered office lease agreement and landlord's written consent
Foreign investment approval letter from MOEAIC
Passports and residence certificates of all directors
Company seal specimen card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended, the registrar will issue a defect notice requiring correction within 15 days. The applicant must amend the deficient documents through the online portal and resubmit. If the application is formally rejected, the Company may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs or commence judicial review in accordance with the Administrative Litigation Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Labor, and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor; local fire and health authorities only if physical premises are used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Company Registration Certificate, the Company must register with the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and business tax. The Company must apply for a Uniform Invoice Number and, where required, approval to issue electronic receipts and e-invoices. The responsible person must file the seal card and identity documents, and the Company must register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration for employee coverage. For pure online retail and print-on-demand sales with no onshore production facility, no additional industrial license is required. If the Company later leases an office, it must undergo local fire safety inspection and comply with occupational safety and health filing requirements.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate issued by MOEA
Uniform Invoice Issuance Application form
Seal impression card and identity card of the responsible person
Registered office lease agreement
Director and shareholder identity documents
Corporate bank account confirmation letter
Tax registration forms and employer insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority imposes a late-registration penalty, the Company may submit an explanatory statement and request abatement or deferred penalty under the applicable tax rules. If the Uniform Invoice application is rejected, correct the registered address or responsible person data and refile within seven days. For labor insurance registration, any defect notice must be cured by submitting amended employee lists and contract evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 is online retailing without physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing in Taiwan
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no mandatory industrial operating permit is required for print-on-demand custom apparel retailing; tax registration and Uniform Invoice issuance constitute the only statutory startup requirements

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (Taiwan EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Exempt; no Category A or Category B EIA project applies to an online retail business, and the company does not operate a factory, fixed pollution source, or hazardous waste facility
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company has no wastewater discharge, air pollutant emission, or hazardous waste generation thresholds to satisfy under the Water Pollution Control Act, Air Pollution Control Act, or Waste Disposal Act; if the company later establishes its own garment printing, dyeing, or fulfillment operation, a fixed pollution source registration, wastewater discharge permit, and hazardous waste manifest would become mandatory

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a home-office or fully outsourced POD retailer; no Civil Defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required. If the Company opens a leased office or fulfillment center, the premises must pass local fire bureau inspection and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including fire extinguisher placement, emergency exits, and risk assessments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); official online filing and registration portal: National Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the China WFOE, the statutory tax identification number is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) obtained under the multi-license integration regime. The WFOE first obtains its business license from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); tax registration is automatically completed by data sharing between SAMR and STA. The non-resident shareholder does not receive a TIN solely through equity ownership; a non-resident enterprise earning China-source income separately registers as a non-resident taxpayer with STA for withholding/collection purposes. The WFOE must then activate its e-Tax account using the legal representative's real-name authentication, complete supplementary resident-enterprise tax registration (accounting policy, responsible officers, banking details, and taxpayer type), apply for general VAT taxpayer status if annual taxable turnover reaches the RMB 5 million threshold, and register for export VAT zero-rating/refund processing before making zero-rated outward sales to Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election, LLC-style entity classification election, or hybrid mismatch election. The only available status option is the VAT small-scale taxpayer vs. general taxpayer election; a below-threshold WFOE may voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer, but this does not alter the default Entity_Level_Taxation treatment for corporate income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC Value-Added Tax Law and its implementing regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in taxable sales over a continuous 12-month period is the mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration threshold; the WFOE is a registered taxpayer in China effective from the date its business license is issued.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates electronic invoicing through the e-Tax platform and the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) regime. VAT special invoices must be generated using STA-issued tax control equipment (tax U-Key) or the FDEI system, and the invoice data are transmitted to the tax authority in real time. Fiscal clearance includes automatic validation of invoice codes and digital tax stamps, anti-fraud matching of sales and input tax data, and mandatory filing of computerized VAT return data before zero-rate export clearance can be processed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Tangible goods physically exported from the PRC customs territory to Taiwan qualify for the 0% VAT rate if the goods leave China under customs supervision, the sale is made to an overseas/Taiwan buyer, and the export proceeds are repatriated to the WFOE. For POD custom apparel, the finished goods must be duly declared for export at a PRC customs point and the entire sales price should be reported as zero-rated export sales in the VAT return; digital service revenues not tied to the physical export are not eligible for goods export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export goods declaration (export release record) generated through the China International Trade Single Window and cleared by the General Administration of Customs of China
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing actual shipment from a PRC port or customs clearance point to Taiwan
Commercial invoice and packing list issued by the WFOE in the name of the Taiwan buyer
Bank foreign exchange collection record under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Monitoring System evidencing inward remittance of export proceeds
Zero-rated export sales declaration and export VAT refund/zero-rate filing submitted through the e-Tax portal with customs data cross-match
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA and the General Administration of Customs perform cross-system audits matching customs release records, export invoices, VAT returns, and SAFE bank receipt records. If export proceeds are not received within the 180-day deadline, the 0% rate is clawed back, the WFOE must pay VAT at the applicable standard rate with late-payment penalties and interest. False declarations or fictitious exports to obtain zero-rating are treated as defrauding export tax refunds, triggering recovery of all refunded tax, penalties ranging from 50% to five times the tax involved under the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection, and, for serious cases, criminal liability under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China including fines and imprisonment of responsible persons.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), with exclusive authority to set foreign exchange policy, manage the New Taiwan dollar, approve licensed FX banks, and enforce the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act and the Act Governing Central Bank of the Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is a managed-float currency, fully convertible on current-account transactions, while capital-account movements are subject to CBC supervision and, for foreign direct investment, prior approval by the Investment Commission. As a Taiwan-registered foreign-invested limited company, the WFOE may receive invested capital only after the applicable cross-strait investment permit is granted; the CBC requires every inbound wire to be processed through an Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank and to carry appropriate purpose codes. Export-related foreign exchange is freely retained in Foreign Currency Deposit Unit (FCDU) accounts, but conversion into NTD must be executed through authorized banks with declaration forms for transactions above the CBC threshold. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permissible after tax settlement; however, dividend distributions paid to a mainland China parent will be subject to the statutory dividend withholding tax and heightened compliance scrutiny. Practically, the largest clearing hurdles remain the Investment Commission approval chain, the CBC's declaration regime, and the need for a Tier-1 local banking sponsor to validate each large or suspicious transaction file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For each export shipment, the exporter must repatriate the foreign-currency sales proceeds to a domestic authorized foreign-exchange bank within four months of customs clearance. There is no mandatory NTD conversion ratio for corporate exporters; one hundred percent of the export proceeds may be retained as a Foreign Currency Deposit balance. If any retained amount is subsequently converted to NTD, the conversion must be executed through an authorized FX bank and must be reported on a Foreign Exchange Declaration Form whenever the transaction exceeds the CBC's current USD 10,000 equivalent threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: NTD Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Deposit (FCD) account
Foreign Currency Deposit Unit (FCDU) account and cross-currency settlement account
Capital escrow account and NTD operating account for inbound investment proceeds
Domestic trade settlement account with SWIFT and LC/collection capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and standard fintech treasury platforms do not hold a Taiwan banking licence and cannot lawfully open entity-level NTD or FCDU deposit accounts for a Taiwan company. Taiwan only permits domestically licensed Electronic Payment Institutions under the Electronic Payment Institution Act to provide certain stored-value services, and foreign EMIs are not eligible as principal bank accounts. Fintech payment aggregators may be used solely as merchant acquiring rails for e-commerce card payments, but all corporate treasury liquidity and FX settlement must run through local Tier-1 banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and authorized signatories are required to appear physically at the Taiwan branch of the Tier-1 bank for the AML/KYC interview and account-opening signing. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted under Taiwan AML practice; only in exceptional cases will a bank consider video-verified opening for an existing international customer, and even then the ultimate beneficial owner must still complete an in-person identity verification. The local general manager may act as signatory only if he or she is properly appointed in a board resolution and appears in person with a valid Taiwan residence permit or work permit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity caused by multilayered mainland China or Hong Kong intermediary shareholders; banks will flag any UBO chain that cannot be wholly documented.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised corporate registry extract of the Taiwan WFOE, complete shareholder register, Hong Kong Companies Registry search if intermediaries exist, certified UBO declaration form, identity documents for every natural-person shareholder above 25 percent, a chain-of-control chart, and audited financial statements of the direct parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and political-exposure screening mismatches on cross-strait directors, shareholders, or financing names, including lookup hits on restrictive watchlists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An executed sanctions/PEP screening consent and waiver, sworn confirmation of no listed ownership, certified passports and proof of address for all directors, adverse-media reports from a commercial due-diligence database, and a written explanatory memorandum covering each screening hit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering suspicion in custom apparel retail due to potential fictitious sales, over/under-invoicing, or mismatched shipping records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of aggregated sales and payout reporting from Stripe and PayPal, a sample bundle of commercial invoices with HS codes, order-level logs, carrier proof-of-delivery records, purchase orders for blank apparel and printing consumables, and bank statements showing supplier payments matching the trade cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and initial capital injection not adequately demonstrated as lawful third-party or parent funding, especially if the investment arrives from mainland China under capital-control approvals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The executed Investment Commission permit and CBC inbound remittance approval, remittance purpose-code evidence, source-of-funds declaration, FATCA and CRS self-certifications, audited statutory financial statements, loan agreement if the capital is debt-funded, and a treasury forecast explaining the use of funds for POD inventory, printing, and platform settlements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from the mainland Chinese parent must first pass through China SAFE foreign exchange direct investment registration and Taiwan Investment Commission approval. The remitter should then send a SWIFT wire using the investment remittance purpose code and the Taiwan WFOE's bank details; the Taiwan authorized bank will produce a Foreign Exchange Settlement Statement. After receipt, the Taiwan WFOE must complete a CBC foreign exchange declaration if the amount exceeds the threshold, and the capital contribution must be formally verified by a Taiwan qualified CPA or notary as part of the company capital/investment verification. No cash withdrawals are permitted; funds must remain in the designated Capital Escrow or Capital Reserve Account until the Investment Commission filing is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outward trade and service payments, the Taiwan WFOE will use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for supplier deposits and service fees, with commercial letters of credit for bulk purchases of apparel blanks and printing equipment where the bank negotiates documents against title, and documentary collections for settlement against shipping documents. Domestic e-commerce revenue settles in NTD through acquiring banks, while cross-border POD disbursements to merchant platforms and overseas sub-warehouses are cleared through the bank's electronic banking system with supporting invoices and FX declaration forms for each outgoing wire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot and outright forward FX contracts for genuine current-account exposures, subject to underlying trade documentation and CBC reporting
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for balance-sheet hedging of foreign-currency loans or investment positions

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts only where underlying trade turnover in NTD/foreign currency is documented and the CBC approves use; speculative NDF positions are prohibited for domestic corporates
Covered vanilla FX options for hedging future receivables and payables, with written risk exposure limits approved by the WFOE board

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular shareholders' meeting adoption and filing of annual business report, financial statements, and distribution proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce / Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular shareholders' meeting must be convened within 6 months after the fiscal year end, i.e. by 30 June for a calendar-year company. The adopted financial statements, business report, and meeting minutes must be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 15 days after adoption.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the regular shareholders' meeting within the statutory window without an approved extension may lead the competent authority to order convening or, upon shareholder petition, to convene the meeting at company expense. A company that remains dormant, has not commenced business within 6 months, or suspends business for 6 months may be administratively dissolved and struck off the corporate register under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax settlement return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance for the registered office district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 May to 31 May of the year following the tax year. For the calendar year 2024 tax year, filing and payment are due by 31 May 2025. If the date falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual return is filed late, a surcharge of 3% is imposed for each month or part month of delay, up to a maximum of 10% of the tax due. Late payment accrues interest at the one-year postal fixed deposit rate. False or concealment-based returns are subject to a penalty of up to 3 times the underpaid tax. Unpaid tax may be transferred after 30 days to the Administrative Enforcement Agency for compulsory attachment, and the responsible person may be subject to an exit restriction in serious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added and non-value-added business tax (VAT) returns and unified invoice filing obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, local governing tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Bimonthly returns must be filed and tax paid by the 15th day of the month following each two-month period: Jan-Feb by 15 Mar; Mar-Apr by 15 May; May-Jun by 15 Jul; Jul-Aug by 15 Sep; Sep-Oct by 15 Nov; Nov-Dec by 15 Jan of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior discovery by the tax authority attracts an overdue penalty of 1% of the tax amount for every two days of delay, capped at 15%; if no tax is payable, a fixed penalty of NT$1,500 to NT$15,000 applies. Continued failure after notices may result in freezing and attachment of bank accounts and property, and prolonged non-operation may trigger administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and control-owner register under Company Act Article 22-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce via the Company Registration and Management Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual online confirmation must be completed by 31 March each year. Any change to directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more of the shares must be reported within 15 days of the occurrence; initial filing is due within 15 days of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Company Act Article 22-1, failure to file, false filing, or failure to correct after a rectification notice is subject to a fine of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000. Repeated or intentional non-disclosure for anti-money-laundering avoidance can lead to revocation of foreign-investment approval and, in severe cases, administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-investment operations report to the Investment Commission, if the foreign-investment approval imposes an annual reporting condition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end, and in any event by 30 June for a calendar-year company, unless the specific approval letter imposes an earlier date. The report should mirror the annual audited or board-approved financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to comply with the foreign-investment reporting condition may suspend the foreign investor's ability to repatriate capital, decrease the credibility of future investment approvals, and, if the company is also non-operating for 6 months, support an MOEA order for dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employee withholding statements and wage-related tax declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual withholding lists for salaries and other payments subject to individual income tax must be filed by 31 January of the year following payment. Monthly or quarterly withholding remittances follow the payment schedule for the period during which the wages were paid.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of withholding statements attracts a penalty of 1% of the withheld amount for each month of delay, capped at 20% of the amount. Failure to remit withheld tax may result in enforcement action and criminal liability for the responsible person.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly labor insurance, national health insurance, and labor pension employer contributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor; National Health Insurance Administration, Ministry of Health and Welfare; Bureau of Labor Funds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employer premiums and labor pension amounts are generally due by the last day of the following month for each payroll month; annual salary base adjustments are reflected in the February/March and August/September recalculation cycles.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent labor insurance and health insurance premiums accrue interest and are subject to compulsory collection; late labor pension deposits may result in administrative fines and surcharge. Prolonged failure to pay employment-related statutory premiums, combined with business inactivity, may support an administrative strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance of statutory registers and filing of registration changes for directors, capital, address, and authorized representatives
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce / Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change to directors, supervisors, company name, registered address, paid-in capital, or business scope must be filed within 15 days of the underlying corporate resolution or event. The registers must be continuously maintained on-site and made available for inspection by MOEA officers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register a reportable change within 15 days may result in a fine of NT$10,000 to NT$500,000 depending on the section violated. A company that cannot show actual operational continuity, records, or statutory registers for a prolonged period becomes vulnerable to MOEA dissolution under Company Act Article 10.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified public accountant audit applies to: (i) all public companies registered with the Financial Supervisory Commission, including listed, OTC-listed, emerging-stock, and TWSE/TPEx-disclosing issuers, regardless of asset or revenue size; (ii) non-public companies limited by shares with paid-in capital of NT$30 million or more (approximately US$937,500 at 32 NTD/USD) under Company Act Article 20, whose annual financial statements must be audited and certified by a Taiwanese CPA and filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; (iii) banks, financial holding companies, bills finance companies, securities firms, futures commission merchants, and insurance enterprises supervised by the Financial Supervisory Commission, with no size exemption; (iv) any enterprise whose foreign-investment approval imposes a CPA audit condition, particularly for capital repatriation or corporate restructuring; and (v) any enterprise, regardless of balance sheet or turnover, when the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the National Taxation Bureau exercises its statutory examination power and orders a CPA examination. There is no fixed headcount trigger for an ordinary print-on-demand apparel retailer under Taiwanese company law; however, an employer with 200 or more employees that establishes a labor pension supervisory committee is separately required to obtain actuary-certified pension calculations, which is not a full financial statement audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies apply International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public companies prepare financial statements under the Business Entity Accounting Act, the Business Entity Accounting Handling Rules, and the generally accepted accounting principles of the Republic of China; they may elect to apply the Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards for small and medium-sized enterprises as adopted by the FSC. The statutory income tax return is prepared on a tax basis reconciling book net income to taxable income. Books and accounts must be maintained in Taiwan and expressed in New Taiwan Dollars.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, every non-public company must file a register of its directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding 10% or more of the issued shares. Initial filing must be submitted to the MOEA Company Registration and Management Information System within 15 days of incorporation, and any subsequent change in ownership or management must be reported within 15 days. In addition, a mandatory annual confirmation window applies by 31 March each year, during which the WFOE must reconfirm all controlling shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners. Where the foreign parent holds, directly or indirectly, 10% or more, the ultimate natural-person beneficial owner must be disclosed. Failure to complete the annual confirmation or the 30-day change-reporting rule triggers an MOEA rectification order and, if uncorrected, fines of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 under Company Act Article 22-1.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Certificates and Transfer Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 2,500 per annum for a registered office address and local corporate secretary or compliance agent; fees increase to USD 1,500 - 3,500 if the agent also administers patent, trademark, or employment documentation. Actual market range varies by city and service provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit fee is incurred if paid-in capital is below NT$30 million. Voluntary compilation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate for High and New Technology Enterprises; reduced rate for Small and Low-Profit Enterprises (a 20% reduced rate on taxable income below a threshold, plus additional exemptions); 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; 15% rate for encouraged industries in the Western Development; tax holidays and expat incentives in certain free trade zones and under the Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework; VAT export zero-rating without full exemption of income taxes; possible patent box regime under local Chinese innovation policies in Shenzhen or Shanghai free trade zones, if applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (A-Type) (Form A01012 / 收入及成本费用明细表 and supporting schedules A000000, A100000, A105000, etc.) filed electronically via the State Taxation Administration E-Tax Filing System (电子税务局 e-Tax System) at www.etax.chinatax.gov.cn
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities, the deadline is May 31 of the following year. Quarterly provisional filings are due 15 days after the end of each quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15), with a final settlement in the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Revenue (营业收入) – total gross income from the sale of goods, provision of services, and other business activities during the tax year, excluding value-added tax (VAT) and before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all print-on-demand e-commerce sales, including domestic and export sales. For non-resident owners, ensure that the WFOE's income attributable to a Chinese permanent establishment (if any) is fully disclosed. Convert foreign currency amounts into RMB using the official exchange rate at the time of receipt. Export sales may be VAT zero-rated but must still be included in gross revenue for corporate income tax (CIT). Cross-border e-commerce income from platforms such as Stripe/PayPal should be reconciled with bank statements and withholding certificates. Do not net out platform fees, payment-processing fees, or refunds; such items belong in operating costs or period expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Costs (营业成本) – costs directly attributable to revenue generation, including raw materials, production machinery, subcontracted printing services, packaging, and freight/inventory costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses supported by valid invoicing and contracts. If the WFOE purchases raw materials from a Taiwanese affiliate, the transaction must satisfy the arm's-length principle. The allocation of direct costs must be consistent with the actual manufacturing and logistics functions performed in China. Do not deduct imputed or overhead costs that are not actually incurred. All cross-border related-party cost-sharing arrangements must be documented in the transfer pricing file; otherwise the expenses may be disallowed and adjusted upward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and Surcharges (税金及附加) – urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty, and other allowable business taxes except VAT and income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Property tax, vehicle tax, and land use tax are not included in this box; they are separately deductible. For a WFOE, the tax authority may scrutinize the logic between total sales and indirect tax surcharges. Ensure that Chinese VAT paid on purchases is not erroneously included; VAT is a pass-through tax and is not deductible for CIT. For cross-border royalties or interest paid to Taiwanese entities, the associated withholding tax is not deductible here; it must be recorded as a nondeductible expense and added back in the tax adjustment schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Period Expenses (销售费用、管理费用、财务费用) – selling expenses (marketing, platform commissions, logistics), general administrative expenses (salaries, rent, office), and financial expenses (interest on borrowings, bank charges).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocation of period expenses between domestic and offshore activities must be made on a consistent basis. Intercompany management fees paid to a Taiwanese parent or affiliate are deductible only if the taxpayer proves that the services were actually rendered, are for the benefit of the WFOE, and the fee is within market range. Interest deducted on shareholder loans is subject to thin-capitalization rules (debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1; 5:1 for banks/financial institutions). The 'beneficial ownership' test must be satisfied for interest withholding purposes. Travel and entertainment expenses are subject to statutory caps (e.g., 60% of entertainment expense limited to 5% of revenue).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before Tax (利润总额) – the net financial result after deducting the above costs and expenses but before tax adjustments; this is the accounting profit before CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile this box with the audited financial statements. If the WFOE has taken advantage of preferential free-zone incentives, compute the effective tax rate net of such incentives. Non-resident shareholders do not directly enter this box, but the amount of distributable profit will trigger a 10% dividend withholding tax upon actual distribution. Losses incurred by the WFOE cannot be used to offset any profits earned by the Taiwanese parent; the carryforward period for domestic losses is five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustments – Additions (纳税调整增加额) – non-deductible expenses, excessive amounts, and adjustments required by law, including penalties, fines, non-compliant related-party payments, entertainment over cap, and thin-capitalization interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any unpaid withholding tax on outbound royalties, interest, or dividends must be added back. Transfer pricing adjustments made unilaterally by the Chinese tax authority will be included in this box. As a WFOE, Brazilian, or other non-resident Chinese-owned entities, be aware that the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) may recharacterize transactions lacking economic substance. For cross-border payments to Taiwan, even if no DTA is in force, the GAAR can still deem the payment as a dividend or otherwise deny bankruptcy of the deduction; ensure full TP documentation is contemporaneous.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustments – Deductions (纳税调整减少额) – allowable deductions not recognized in financial accounting, such as R&D super deduction, accelerated depreciation on qualified equipment, tax-exempt domestic dividends, and certain investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the 100% super deduction for qualified R&D expenditures incurred in China; if the R&D is partly performed offshore by a Taiwanese contract research organization, retain detailed contracts and evidence of actual work performed in China to avoid disallowance. Dividends received from Chinese resident subsidiaries are exempt, but dividends received from outside China are not so exempt. For the print-on-demand platform, any qualifying e-commerce infrastructure investment could be eligible for a special tax credit under local incentive regimes; document all facts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss Carryforward (弥补以前年度亏损) – offset current taxable income with losses incurred in prior years within the statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses allowed under Chinese law are eligible. Losses arising from foreign branches or from a previously split-off Taiwanese operations are not allowed. The five-year limitation applies; for High and New Technology Enterprises, the statute can be extended to ten years. If the WFOE has consistent losses while demonstrating profitability to its Taiwanese parent, tax authorities may investigate potential profit-shifting via transfer pricing or failure to maintain economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income (应纳税所得额) – the final tax base after all adjustments and loss carryforwards, to which the CIT rate is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable income computed here is the basis for the statutory tax liability. For a non-resident parent company, this amount is not taxed directly at the corporate level but indirectly upon dividend distributions through the 10% withholding tax. Ensure that any permanent establishment attribution or profit attribution to the Taiwanese group is correctly reflected in the TP documentation. If taxable income is artificially reduced to zero, the tax authority may invoke a deemed taxation or anti-abuse challenge under the 'economic substance' doctrine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable Tax Rate (适用税率) – 25% standard rate, or preferential rates (e.g., 15% for qualified High-New Tech Enterprises) if the entity holds valid certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE holds an HNTE certificate, attach the certificate and ensure the standards (e.g., R&D expenditure ratio, headcount, technical personnel ratio) are updated annually. The withholding obligation distribution to the Taiwanese shareholder is not linked to this rate; even if the corporate rate is 15%, the dividend withholding is still 10% (assuming no treaty relief). The same rule applies for domestic branch profits remitted abroad; they are subject to 10% divorce tax under Article 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income Tax Payable (应纳所得税额) – the product of taxable income and the applicable rate, after deducting tax credits such as equipment investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that the quarterly provisional payments are reconciled with the annual liability. Any excess provisional payments will be refunded or carried forward. Non-resident investors with repatriated China profits are not entitled to any income tax credit for Chinese CIT paid at the WFOE level; they are separate taxpayers. The WFOE's payment of a distribution will trigger withholding tax, which must be filed within seven days of the date of distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final Settlement of Tax (应补/退税额) – the difference between annual tax liability and sum of quarterly prepayments; this amount is either payable with the annual return or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that the tax withholding certificates issued by the WFOE on distributions to the Taiwanese parent are accurate. If a refund is claimed due to overpayment, a tax audit may be triggered into the absent deduction treatment of prior adjustments. Non-resident shareholders may face difficulties retrieving refunded CIT if the WFOE's accounting books are not fully compliant, so maintain a permanent filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: Under Article 62 of the Taxation Administration Law (TAL), from 2,000 to 10,000 RMB (or 2,000-50,000 RMB for serious cases). Additional late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the outstanding tax per day is applied under Article 32. Under Article 63, understating taxable income or fraudulent filing will trigger a civil penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax, and possible criminal exposure under Article 201 of the Criminal Law for tax evasion (unpaid tax exceeding 50,000 RMB and 10%+ of taxable amount, imprisonment up to 7 years). Failure to maintain TP documentation may incur a penalty up to 50,000 RMB under SAT Announcement No. 42 of 2016, plus penalty interest under special tax adjustments.
